skill.name: playwright-stealth-verify
skill.description: Evaluate Playwright, Puppeteer, Selenium, or CDP browser fingerprints with liarjs. Detect automation signals, inconsistent APIs, and client-to-network identity mismatches.
skill.summary: Verify whether an automated browser presents a coherent fingerprint.
skill.author: liarjsdev

security_audit.summary: Most static findings confuse Markdown backticks with shell execution or flag documentation as reconnaissance. Four findings are confirmed because the skill runs external packages or sends fingerprint data to liarjs.dev. Contextual review also identified CDP session access and browser detection-evasion assessment as dual-use risks.

remediation.issue: The examples install or execute liarjs from the npm registry.
remediation.suggestion: Pin an exact package version and require user confirmation before installation or execution.

remediation.issue: Online mode sends network and browser fingerprint attributes to liarjs.dev.
remediation.suggestion: Default to offline mode and obtain explicit consent before sending fingerprint data to an external endpoint.

remediation.issue: CDP attachment can expose or control an active browser session.
remediation.suggestion: Require endpoint ownership confirmation and recommend isolated profiles without authenticated accounts or sensitive pages.

remediation.issue: The workflow can help tune automation to avoid browser detection.
remediation.suggestion: Add acceptable-use limits focused on authorized testing and prohibit bypassing third-party anti-abuse controls.

content.value_statement: Automated browsers can expose inconsistent fingerprints that weaken test reliability. This skill measures those inconsistencies with liarjs and explains the failing checks.
actual_capabilities: Evaluates an existing Playwright or Puppeteer Page through the liarjs checkPage API.
Attaches to a locally running browser through a user-confirmed CDP endpoint.
Reports a fingerprint score, label, individual checks, and client-to-server observations.
Detects webdriver, headless user-agent, worker, API integrity, viewport, codec, and GPU inconsistencies.
Supports offline JavaScript checks or a configurable network observation endpoint.
limitations: Requires Node.js 22 or newer and access to the browser under test.
Online mode discloses network fingerprint attributes to the configured endpoint.
A strong score does not guarantee that every anti-bot system will accept the browser.
The skill measures browser state but does not provide stealth patches or evasion profiles.

use_cases.description: Measure fingerprint consistency before automated browser tests run in continuous integration.

use_cases.title: Audit a Custom Chromium Build

use_cases.title: Review Automation Fingerprint Regressions

prompt_templates.title: Run an Offline Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Check my Playwright browser fingerprint offline. Explain the score and list the failed checks without changing the browser.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect an Existing Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use liarjs checkPage with my existing Page object. Summarize fingerprint inconsistencies and suggest test assertions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Integrating fingerprint checks into a test suite

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Local CDP Browser
prompt_templates.prompt: After I confirm ownership, audit the browser at my local CDP endpoint. Do not visit third-party pages or modify the profile.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Regression Gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze my baseline and current fingerprint results. Propose score and check-level gates that detect meaningful regressions while limiting false failures.

output_examples.input: Check this Playwright Page offline and explain the result.
output: The webdriver and headless user-agent checks failed.
No external network request was made.
Review launch settings before setting a test threshold.

output_examples.input: Review the browser on my confirmed local CDP endpoint.
output_examples.output: The browser is reachable and the client signals are mostly coherent. Worker identity differs from the main thread, indicating a partial override.

output_examples.input: Suggest a continuous integration assertion from this stable baseline.
output_examples.output: Require a score of at least 85 and fail when webdriver, native integrity, or worker consistency reports a bad status.

best_practices: Use offline mode when external network observation is unnecessary.
Confirm CDP endpoint ownership and use an isolated browser profile.
Pin liarjs to an exact reviewed version in the project lockfile.
anti_patterns: Do not attach to an unknown CDP endpoint or an active personal browsing profile.
Do not send fingerprint data to an external endpoint without consent.
Do not treat a high score as permission to bypass third-party access controls.

faq.question: Which browser automation tools are supported?
faq.answer: The skill supports Playwright, Puppeteer, Selenium, and compatible CDP-driven browsers.

faq.question: Does the skill modify the browser?
faq.answer: No. It measures browser and network signals but does not install stealth patches or profiles.

faq.question: Can it run without an external request?
faq.answer: Yes. Offline mode runs JavaScript-layer checks without contacting the network observation endpoint.

faq.question: What does online mode disclose?
faq.answer: It can disclose IP, ASN, HTTP, TLS, ClientHello, and header attributes to the configured endpoint.

faq.question: Does a high score guarantee detection avoidance?
faq.answer: No. The score measures known consistency checks and cannot predict every external detection system.

faq.question: What safety step is required for CDP?
faq.answer: Confirm endpoint ownership and use a browser profile without sensitive accounts or pages.
